newsitem.title: ITALY: Versace veers off at hem, takes ruff with smooth.
newsitem.headline: Versace veers off at hem, takes ruff with smooth.

text.p: Italy's Gianni Versace played havoc with hemlines in his 1997 spring/summer designs at the Milan fashion shows and added a few feminine flounces to a vibrant, uptempo collection.
Versace said he wanted his style to be "rock classic -- for women who loved dressing dynamically.
He opened his show late on Saturday with a black-and-white rock video of pop artist Elton John before launching supermodel Naomi Campbell onto the catwalk in a little grey outfit.

Then came little black, white and lilac numbers with ruffles edging deep-cut backs scooped low like a classic swimsuit, tiny ruffles finishing skirts at the knee or larger ones falling flirtatiously from hemlines cut at acute and gentle diagonals.

Dresses followed the bodyline smoothly without becoming tight. Many had tiny shoulder straps and were worn with dramatically high open-toed wedge-heeled shoes or slender high heels with slightly built-up soles.
Versace said his woman for summer 1997 was "eccentric, a woman whose personality doesn't change just because her clothes do, a woman who knows how to move well in life -- Lolita's daughter."

His reference to the seduced and seductive teenager of Vladimir Nabokov's novel "Lolita" was reflected in lacy tops, sheer panelling, tiny frills and short see-through swinging nightdress-style garments.

Evening wear included ankle-length sheaths with long sleeves, backs cut low to the base of the spine and a trailing rear hemline, lacy-bodiced high-waisted gowns in pink, lilac, black or grey as well as a wide-meshed net dress in black with a filmy black underslip and ruffled hem.

Versace mostly went for more strategic transparency than some designers displaying at Milan, with white or black knee- and full-length gowns opaque at the bodice and skirt but with an angled or trailing hemline and a crescent-shaped transparent panel across the navel and down the thigh.

More elaborate lace came with a full-length grey gown worn by Campbell. It had net panels in the skirt delicately decorated in the style of a wedding veil and trimmed at the hip with several rows of tiny ruffles.

Along with Versace's hallmark bright lilac, he flashed characteristically strong sunshine yellow, emerald green and vibrant red in his collection and decked the models out with flowers and leaves in their hair.
Blonde-haired Texan model Jerry Hall, wife of Rolling Stones rock star Mick Jagger, earlier made a surprise appearance on the catwalk for fashion label Iceberg.
Italian media said actress Sofia Loren would be among the guests at the presentation of top designer Giorgio Armani's main collection at the close of the Milan shows on Sunday.
